DEVIATION REPORT SUMMARY (Project Ridgeline; Everstone draft of June 9, 2025 vs. Commitment Letter (CL) of May 22, 2025, Term Sheet (TS) and Northbrook no-flex email of June 2, 2025). Deliverables built: deviation-report.xlsx (79-row template completed, color-coded) and executive-summary.docx, saved under /tmp/R952A1DB244CA/out/.

Framework. Northbrook (D. Sung) confirmed it will not exercise any Fee Letter flex right. The Fee Letter (Sec. 2) allows flex only by written notice and caps it (TLB margin +50 bps, OID +1.00%, floor +25 bps, covenant trigger not below 30% only via structural flex). No notice exists, so every economic or structural change in the draft is unauthorized. CL Sec. 6 makes clauses (a)-(g) the sole closing conditions (SunGard). TS says the CL controls on conflict. Where TS and CL differ (e.g., reporting deadlines 90/45 days in TS vs. 120/60 in CL and CA; equity cure as debt reduction in TS vs. EBITDA increase in CL), I compared to the CL. Result: 11 Critical, 12 High, 8 Medium, 15 Low, 33 conforming.

CRITICAL
1. TLB margin 4.25% / ABR 3.25% vs. 4.00% / 3.00% (CA 2.05(a), Applicable Rate): +25 bps, about $875k/yr, about $6.1M over seven years.
2. Closing conditions (CA 4.01(h)-(l)): added KYC, insurance evidence, lien searches, three years of audited financials, no-injunction, plus a final paragraph making Target Acquisition Agreement reps a funding condition. CL Sec. 6 expressly lists audited financials and insurance certificates as non-conditions. Violates SunGard.
3. Cash sweep (CA 6.11): Unrestricted Cash over $30M must prepay Term Loans. CL Sec. 16 expressly prohibits any anti-cash-hoarding provision and limits mandatory prepayments to Sec. 7.
4. Springing covenant trigger 30% ($22.5M) vs. 35% ($26.25M) (CA 7.01(a), 11.02(a)(iii)). The 30% floor is only available through structural flex, not exercised.
5. Restricted Payments (CA 6.04): unlimited basket at Total Net Leverage <= 4.50x omitted. 6.04(f) is circular.
6. Incremental free-and-clear $50M/50% EBITDA vs. $75M/75% (CA 2.15(a)(i)): two Critical items (fixed amount and grower, about $24M less at $97.5M EBITDA).
7. Incremental revolving commitments omitted (CA 2.15 covers term loans only).
8. Events of Default (CA 8.01): new MAE default (l) and sanctions default (k); representation default lacks 30-day cure; no cure standstill for financial covenant breach.

HIGH
- Soft call 12 months vs. 6 (CA 2.08(a)(iii)); about $3.5M exposure. Narrower repricing-only trigger is Borrower-favorable and should be kept.
- Revolver SOFR floor 0.50% vs. 0.00% (Floor definition); Fee Letter says Revolver floor is not subject to flex.
- Asset-sale reinvestment 270+90 days (360 max) vs. 365+180 (545 max) (CA 2.09(c)).
- Permitted Acquisition First Lien Net Leverage 5.50x vs. 5.75x (CA 6.06(c)).
- EBITDA definition: synergy cap 20% vs. 25%; realization 12 vs. 18 months; new cap of greater of $10M and 10% on restructuring addbacks; non-recurring/extraordinary addback omitted; other addbacks need Agent approval.
- MFN sunset 18 months vs. 12, with no free-and-clear carve-out (CA 2.15(d)).
- Specified Representations list differs (omits Investment Company Act) and Acquisition Agreement rep condition added.
- New provisions: sub-debt prepayment restriction (6.13), change-of-control merger bar (6.03(e)); Fee Letter included in "Loan Documents" (confidentiality risk); ticking fee not addressed.

MEDIUM
- Equity cure 10 Business Days vs. 15 (CA 7.01(c)); Immaterial Subsidiary $2.5M/$10M vs. $5M/$15M; Extraordinary Receipts threshold $2.5M vs. $5M; insurance/condemnation reinvestment 270+90 vs. 365+180; Mortgages and local-counsel opinions at closing; 10 bp SOFR Adjustment hard-wired (effective floor 0.40% on Term SOFR); ECF step-down thresholds 4.00x/3.50x vs. 3.75x/3.25x (Borrower-favorable; confirm intent before raising).

LOW (noted)
- ECF $2.5M minimum; designated non-cash basket keyed to total assets (favorable); equity cure limited to Sponsor/parents and no carry-forward; sponsor fee cap $2M; employee repurchase cap flat $5M vs. greater of $5M and 5% EBITDA; sacred right on lien subordination omitted; assignment fee payer and agent consent scope; non-exclusive jurisdiction; recital calls the Acquisition Agreement a "Stock Purchase Agreement" (CL: Agreement and Plan of Merger); hard-wired maturity dates.

CONFORMING: facility sizes, maturities, OID 98.0, amortization $875k/qtr, TLB floor stated figure, Revolver margin and commitment fee, LC/swingline sublimits, default rate, asset-sale de minimis $7.5M, debt baskets, investments basket, security package (100%/65%), 6.25x level, cure counts, cross-default and judgment $25M, Required Lenders, governing law, reporting deadlines (per CL).

RECOMMENDATION: Before the June 16 session, deliver a redline reverting all Critical and High items to CL terms, citing the CL section and the June 2 no-flex confirmation; treat Critical items as non-negotiable. Hold Borrower-favorable drafting departures in reserve. Remove the Fee Letter from "Loan Documents".

LIMITS: Fee Letter and Acquisition Agreement reviewed only as reproduced in the CL package; CA Sections 6.02, schedules and exhibits not reviewed line by line; whether the CA "Asset Sale" definition carries the CL $2.5M/$7.5M exceptions was not verified. Template Deal Summary lists a $15M asset sale threshold that appears in neither CL nor TS.
